content:
Key observations from the test image:
- Soybean stems near soil level
- White cottony/fluffy mold growth on stems
- Distinct black sclerotia (hard, irregularly shaped black bodies) embedded in the white mold
- Bleached, tan-white stem tissue

This strongly points to **White Mold** (Sclerotinia stem rot). Let me confirm with reference images.
White Mold reference matches well: white fluffy mycelium on stems. Anthracnose shows dried brown/dark stems - not a match. Let me view Diaporthe and Rhizoctonia as alternatives.

Diaporthe and Rhizoctonia don't show white fluffy mold - clearly don't match. The test image features are definitively:
- White cottony mycelium on stems
- Hard black sclerotia embedded in the mold
- Bleached stem tissue

**Initial prediction: White_Mold**

Now checking the Attractor Guide.
White_Mold is over-predicted (8x). I must check alternatives: Phomopsis (4x), Tobacco_Streak_Virus (2x), Charcoal_Rot (1x).

Phomopsis shows pod/seed symptoms (shriveled pods, dark spots) - no white mold. Charcoal_Rot shows bleached gray stems with tiny microsclerotia internally - no fluffy white mycelium visible externally.

Neither alternative matches the test image. The test image has unambiguous White Mold signatures:
- Prominent white fluffy/cottony mycelium on stems
- Large hard black sclerotia embedded in the mold
- Bleached stem tissue at nodes

Alternatives from Attractor Guide (Phomopsis = pod/seed disease, Charcoal_Rot = tiny internal microsclerotia without external white mold) do not fit the visible features."}
